description: Test files that exist in this repository and are NOT executed by the pull-request gate. Every entry is a hole in what a green pull request means, stated so that a reader of that green knows what it does not cover, and stated alongside the job that DOES execute the file so a debt is not confused with an absence.
whyThisFileExists: apps/web/playwright.config.ts gates tests/e2e/authenticated/** behind ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH === '1'. For the whole of P1-27 no workflow set it, so the repository's ONLY end-to-end tenant-isolation proof and its ONLY route-level accessibility proof had never once executed anywhere but on the Owner's machine, while `test:web-e2e` reported a green browser tier and the phase records counted browser coverage. Nothing said so anywhere. This file, the LOUD job-summary step in .github/workflows/_reusable-node-quality.yml that reads it, and tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts are what replaced that silence.
whatChangedAndWhatDidNot: The tier is now WIRED and RUN: the `authenticated-browser` job in .github/workflows/protected-develop-verification.yml starts the Supabase stack with the vendored CLI, bootstraps the real operator and the second tenant through scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/create-owner-account.mjs, starts the production API build as a database login that holds neither SUPERUSER nor BYPASSRLS, and runs `npm run test:web-e2e-authenticated` with ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH=1 — then FAILS unless every authenticated spec file contributed at least one executed test. The earlier claim recorded here, that a hosted runner cannot be given a live Supabase, a live API and a real account, was false: a hosted runner has Docker and the Supabase CLI is a devDependency of this repository. It is also reachable BEFORE a merge: the workflow_dispatch trigger takes a `candidate-sha`, and the job refuses to run unless the commit it resolved is exactly that one, so a pull request candidate can be tested and quoted without merging it first. What did NOT change is the pull-request gate itself: no job on pr-ci.yml runs this tier, so a green pull request still does not include it.
hostedObservation: OBSERVED, and it FAILED — honestly recorded rather than rounded up. Run 31337158296 (workflow_dispatch on remediation/p1-27-final-canonical-blockers, commit 155a5f55fdd5b6262ea2ed9c421dcf98f5bc83a7, job `authenticated-browser`) is the first hosted execution of this tier in the repository's history, and it is a PRE-MERGE run, which is what the trigger was extended for. What it settles: a hosted runner does stand the stack up. `supabase start`, `supabase:reset` across every migration and seed, the identity-provider settings read from the CLI, `/auth/v1/health` answering, the Playwright browser install and all five acceptance identities each succeeded. What it found: the bootstrap then failed at scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/create-owner-account.mjs:607, because `alignLocalJwtSigning` recreates the GoTrue container (align-local-jwt.mjs:119-126, `docker rm -f` then `docker run -d`) and `assertHs256` probes the token endpoint once with no retry (align-local-jwt.mjs:140); the recreate returned at 21:38:21.029 and the probe failed with 502 at 21:38:21.039, ten milliseconds later. That is a readiness race in the acceptance bootstrap, not the algorithm refusal its error text blames, and not a limitation of hosted CI. The tier therefore executed ZERO tests and the zero-test guard in this job correctly failed the run rather than reporting green. Until a run exists in which the tier actually executes its specs, these entries stand as written rather than as repaid.
policy: An entry here is a debt, not a dispensation. It must name what the pull-request gate does not prove, why that job does not run it, which job does, what remains unrepaid, what compensates today, and a date by which the arrangement is revisited. tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts fails when a spec is neither executed by the pull-request gate nor declared here, when a declared spec IS executed by the pull-request gate (a declaration must not be able to hide a runnable tier), when a field is missing, when the named executing job does not exist in the workflow it names, and when reviewBy has passed.
howToClose: Two steps, in order. First, observe the `authenticated-browser` job actually EXECUTE its specs and pass — pre-merge by workflow_dispatch with a candidate-sha, then on a protected push — and record both runs. The first hosted attempt (run 31337158296) failed before the tier collected anything, so no execution has yet been observed. Second, put it under a gate: add it to DECLARED_JOBS in scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs and to the `needs` of both `protected-gate` and `ci-gate`, which requires the job to exist in pr-ci.yml as well and therefore requires the job counts in docs/engineering/ci-automation/pull-request-body.md to be updated in the same commit. Only when a gate governs the result may these entries be deleted. Removing an entry without doing that fails tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts, because the spec would then be neither gate-covered nor declared.

unrun.whatItProves: That a signed-in operator of one tenant cannot see another tenant's records through the browser, and that a Tenant A bearer token is refused Tenant B records by the running API.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Tenant isolation is proved at the database layer by the RLS matrix and at the API layer by the backend suite. It is NOT proved end to end through a real session in a real browser by any job a pull request runs, which is the only layer a customer experiences.
unrun.whyThePullRequestGateDoesNotRunIt: It needs a live Supabase GoTrue, a live API on port 3000 and a real account with a real password. Standing those up costs roughly forty minutes of runner time, and the hosted clean room cannot host them: it binds a bare postgres:17-alpine on 54322, which is the exact port scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/context.mjs pins the acceptance database to.
unrun.executedBy: .github/workflows/protected-develop-verification.yml job `authenticated-browser` — on every push to develop and main, and before a merge by workflow_dispatch pinned to a candidate-sha.
unrun.remainingDebt: That job is not in `protected-gate`'s `needs`, so protected-gate can be green while this check is red. DECLARED_JOBS in scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs is shared with pr-ci.yml, so governing it there requires the same job on the pull-request gate and an update to the job counts in docs/engineering/ci-automation/pull-request-body.md.
unrun.compensatingControl: tests/db RLS matrix (critical level, run in both the clean room and database-security) and the backend authorization suite. The Owner acceptance run executes this spec by hand on a machine that has the full local stack.

unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Component-level accessibility is covered by the web unit tier. Whole-page accessibility of authenticated routes — landmark structure, heading order, focus order across a real navigation — is proved by nothing a pull request runs.
